annotation.title_clean: Criminal Liability Arising from Offenses Committed by Robots
annotation.title_en: Criminal Liability Arising from Offenses Committed by Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Al-Jizani, H.K.A.; Heidari, M.; Ali, H.H.; Saeedi, Y.
annotation.venue: The Encyclopedia of Comparative Jurisprudence and Law
annotation.summary_en: Analytical legal article arguing that traditional criminal law, built on material and mental elements, cannot address offenses by autonomous robots. It calls for new liability models combining criminal and technical responsibility, joint responsibility among designers, developers and users, and conditional legal personality for robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Traditional criminal law norms are insufficient for crimes by autonomous robots.
Criminal theory needs reconstruction, not just textual amendment.
Boundaries between criminal, technical and industrial fault are unclear; hybrid liability models are needed.
Legal personhood for robots is theoretically possible under strict conditions.
New rules should define joint responsibility of designers, developers and users, with penalties scaled to robot autonomy.
